name: sidebar
description: Collapsible application sidebar with three modes — expanded, rail (icons only), and a mobile off-canvas drawer — switched responsively and toggled from the keyboard

changes.note: Nested components keep their own parts. The stylesheet reached every part with descendant selectors, so a dropdown in the footer had its trigger styled as the sidebar toggle and its items as nav entries, and rail mode hid every label below the root. Parts are now root > panel > header / nav / footer, header > brand and trigger, nav or footer > item > icon and label. The trigger may also be the root's own child: a drawer that is off-canvas is opened from outside its panel. The rail chevron rule follows the trigger. Every part rule is now a child chain from the root, with the hops in :where(), so no rule changes specificity. No change for markup that follows the template.

Only the sidebar's own triggers toggle it. The controller took every [data-part="trigger"] inside the root, so a dropdown in the footer had its aria-expanded overwritten on every render and its click put the sidebar in rail. Triggers are now matched by owner, looking through layout primitives, and overlay and panel are taken as direct children.

The trigger glyph follows the state: authored once pointing inline-start, the stylesheet mirrors it (`scale: -1 1`, reduced-motion safe) in rail, so a toggled sidebar no longer shows a stale chevron. Both examples carry the one stable label "Toggle sidebar" instead of "Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar", which went stale on the first toggle and contradicted aria-expanded.
Stack the brand glyph and toggle in rail mode so both fit inside the 3.75rem column without unreachable inline-start clipping.

overlay.description: Backdrop shown behind the panel when the mobile drawer is open; click to close

panel.description: The sidebar surface itself — the focus-trap container in drawer mode. Should carry aria-label

header.description: Top area holding the brand and the toggle button

brand-icon.description: Brand glyph; stays visible in rail mode

brand-label.description: Brand wordmark; hidden in rail mode

trigger.description: Toggle button, in the panel's header or as the root's own child (outside the panel, so an off-canvas drawer can be opened). Give it one stable aria-label ("Toggle sidebar") — its aria-expanded tracks the live state, and a button with aria-expanded must not change its name. Author its glyph (an svg or data-ui="icon" child) pointing inline-start, at the collapse; the stylesheet mirrors it in rail. External buttons may also target the sidebar via data-sidebar-toggle="{id}".

item.description: A navigation entry (icon + label). Mark the current page with aria-current="page". In rail mode give it an aria-label since the text label is hidden

icon.description: Item glyph; stays visible in rail mode

label.description: Item text; hidden in rail mode

footer.description: Pinned bottom area (secondary links, user block)

breakpoint.description: Max-width in px below which the sidebar switches to the mobile drawer (matchMedia (max-width: Npx))

keyboard.Enter/Space: activate the toggle button (expanded ↔ rail on desktop, open ↔ close on mobile)
keyboard.Tab: cycle focus within the panel while the mobile drawer is open
keyboard.Shift+Tab: reverse-cycle focus within the panel while the mobile drawer is open

notes: data-state is the single source of truth: expanded | rail | drawer (mobile closed) | drawer-open (mobile open).
Agents can set the initial state declaratively; the controller reconciles it with the current breakpoint on init.
Every toggle button's aria-expanded tracks the live state (labels shown on desktop, drawer open on mobile).
The trigger's accessible name is stable across states ("Toggle sidebar"); the direction is carried by aria-expanded, and visually by the glyph the stylesheet mirrors in rail.
While the mobile drawer is closed the off-screen panel is inert + aria-hidden, so its links never sit in the tab order.
The mobile drawer traps focus, locks body scroll, closes on Escape or overlay click, and returns focus to the opener.
